source: scripts/compare_tab_audio.py flags, reviewed by two agents (compare/agent_verdicts.csv)
rule: tab note: the acoustic reviewer calls it wrong (blind benchmark: 14 of 16 such calls right); missing note: both reviewers call it real (3 of 4)

edits.why: In the same re-strum, C4 and A3 are re-attacked (posteriors 0.75-0.77), but F#4 shows no stem rise (+0.3 against the rendering's +6.5). fl and gaps are 0.13 and 0.07, Basic Pitch does not see it, and the residual is louder at F#4. The only support (gaps_paper 0.53) follows residual leakage, as it does in bar 25 (repeat bar 73 lacks both).

The onset energy peaks a semitone lower (B3 4.9 dB against C4 1.8 dB), and gaps favours B3 (0.78 against 0.19). In the repeats the same spot is B3 with C4 posteriors at about 0.01, and B3 fits the G#dim7 (G#-B-D-F) passing chord; C4 does not.

Across the supposed onset the stem at 62 keeps decaying (-5.6, -8.5, -12.5, -15, -20 dB from 15.90 to 16.12) while Bb3 (58) rises to 6.6 dB. So only Bb3 is re-struck, and the D4 energy is the tail of the earlier chord or G2's overtone. In repeat bars 1, 33 and 65 the D4 at this beat reads about 0 to +5 dB with posteriors of about 0.85.

The stem's F#4 level stays flat at about -6 dB from 21.70 to 21.93 with no harmonic rises (h2 78, h4 90 flat), whereas the re-struck C4 and A3 reach about 0.8 on all models. Only gaps_paper fires (0.60), exactly where the residual has a large F#4 onset (+27 dB, 4 dB louder than the stem), so this looks like the earlier F#4 still ringing plus leakage.

The stem's B3 bin (0.5 dB) is about 8 dB above what the rendering's loud G3 bleeds into it. B3 partials h5 (87, +20 dB) and h3 (78, +7.6 dB) rise, the residual is 18 dB lower, and fl gives 0.48. Repeat bar 76 has B3+G3 at this sixteenth, but two models stay low, so the note is weak.

After the chord's broadband attack, the stem shows no F#4 peak: 66 sits at -11 to -13 dB (about 8-9 dB below the rendering), level with neighbouring bins and explained by F#2's h4. A plucked string-1 note would sustain. Posteriors are mixed (0.58/0.08/0.37), and the residual is louder at 66 on the attack.

The stem has a trough at Eb3 at the attack and 16-19 dB less than the rendering in the sustain (-16 to -18.5 dB vs +0.5), so no Eb3 is ringing. The octave above (63) keeps a sustained local excess, and two models put the onset at Eb4 (0.56/0.75) versus only gaps_paper at Eb3.
edits.note: reviewer's fix was 51 -> 63, but with 63 the chord (F#2 Bb3 C4 Eb4) is unplayable and the fingering drops the unflagged C4; only the removal of 51 is applied

edits.why: The stem has a clear pitched event peaked at B3 (8.9 dB, +20 dB rise, about 120 ms) that is absent in the residual (-24 dB) and in the rendering. It also fills the usual 2.3 chord slot (62/59 at 1.3). Model posteriors are low (0.27) because the note is short and damped.

B3 attacks strongly at 39.07-39.11 (+19 dB), but F4 shows only a gentle swell (+3 dB) that 64 and 66 share and a continuous band carried over from F3's second harmonic. There is no fresh F4 onset; only fl (0.67) fires, while gaps and gaps_paper give 0.00-0.08.

The stem's A3 level falls from about +5.8 dB to -4.7 dB right at 40.50 s, so the note is being damped, not re-plucked (fundamental rise -6.2 dB). Basic Pitch finds no onset, and there is no A3 onset nearby either (posterior 0.03 at 40.67 s), so a timing fix does not apply.

Unlike the clear G3s at 41.43 and 41.89 s, where all three models give G3 and 0 for Ab3, here gaps and gaps_paper give Ab3 0.88/0.61 and G3 about 0. At the attack the Ab3 bin is at or above the G3 bin, as in the stem's real Ab3+D4 chords in bars 13, 29 and 77. That same Bb7 shape (x1x13x) is what this player uses elsewhere. Some G3 energy follows the attack (fl and Basic Pitch say G3), so this is not certain.

The real F4 pedal notes (40.67, 41.88, 42.18, 42.56 s) show a clear peak at 65 that is 3-4 dB above both neighbours, and all models give about 0.8. Here the energy at 65 is only the broadband strum transient: it is no higher than 64, falls to -11 to -15 dB within 70 ms while the D4 holds, and the models give only 0.21/0.47/0.08. This fits the player's Bb7 voicing without F4.

The Eb4 fundamental rises only 12 dB, the same as the Ab2 bass partials struck at the same moment, and Eb4 is exactly the bass's 3rd harmonic. Eb4's own harmonics show no rise (Eb5 -27.7 dB, falling by 6 dB). The real Eb4 on the same string and fret at 46.17 s rises 24-37 dB across all harmonics. Only one model fires (fl 0.61), but even the rendering's Eb4 is barely detected (0.04), so this is uncertain.

The stem's A3 falls to -5.4 dB at 46.36 s and then jumps to +12.6 dB at 46.40-46.46 s (a 22 dB rise), with rises at harmonics 2-6. There is no A2 fundamental at that moment (-15 dB), so it is not the next bass note's overtone. The residual is 17 dB weaker. The picture shows a clear re-attack of A3 on beat 1.4.

The energy at C4 is 6.3 dB below the C3 bass, which is weaker than the C3 octave partial alone gives in this stem (1-2 dB below the fundamental at 44.66 and 45.43 s). So no extra C4 is added. Basic Pitch finds no C4, while the chord's C3, G3 and E4 are all detected at about 0.8-0.9. gaps and gaps_paper give 0.00/0.13, whereas the rendering's C4 scores 0.75.

G3 has a strong new onset: +17 dB at the fundamental and +28.6 dB at G4 (h2). Two models give high posteriors (gaps 0.85, fl 0.67), Basic Pitch detects it, and the stem is about 15 dB above the residual. No G2 or C2 is sounding, so it is not an overtone.

Stem E3 rises 9.5 dB to 0 dB, with rises at h2, h4 and h5, while the residual at 52 is 12 dB lower and falling. There is no new E2 onset to make it an overtone. gaps gives 0.87, identical to the played E3 at the same beat 2.2 in repeat bars 12 and 28, and the level matches those notes.

Only fl sees G4 (0.64); gaps and gaps_paper give 0.00, and the stem's 67 bin shows no level change beyond the decaying F#4 next to it (no rise at h2). The residual has a G4 onset at this exact moment (+15.5 dB) and is louder than the stem, so this is likely leakage. The descending sequence with bar 84's F4 makes the note musically plausible, so confidence is low.

D3 in the stem is only -14.9 dB, about 27 dB below G3. That matches the no-D3 strum at 78.54 (-12.6 dB), not the real open D3 at 83.105 (-4.4 dB, all models above 0.75). fl and gaps give 0.04, and the residual rises at D3 at the same time. The tab's 20 ms duration also points to a blip.

gaps gives 0.87 and fl 0.41. The stem's G#3 bin overtakes the ringing G3 at about 83.60, and it is 6.6 dB above the rendering while the other chord tones match. G#3 is not a harmonic of Eb3, C#4 or F4. It completes the 1-2-1 fingering on strings 1-3 that the tab uses for 65/61/56 in bar 106.

In the stem, energy at 55-56 falls to about -8 dB at 83.90-83.95, then comes back to about +2 dB from 84.00 to 84.15. That makes it a new note, not one still ringing, and its spectral shape matches the stem's Ab3 at 84.30. Neither the rendering (-20 dB) nor the residual (-23 dB after the drum transient) has it, and it is not a harmonic of the C3 bass. Basic Pitch and the fl model (0.49) also mark it, but the gaps models do not.

At 87.95 the stem has a clear peak at 55 (8.4 dB, +12-14 dB rise, 54/56 lower). The rendering is at -11 dB there and the residual at -20 dB. It is well above what the fading G2's second harmonic could give, and no tab note has a harmonic there. Basic Pitch detects 55 at the chord.

The stem has a strong new peak at 55 (9.5 dB, +20 dB rise, 54/56 about 3 dB lower). The rendering is at -17 dB and the residual at -5 dB, and it is not a harmonic of the F2 bass. The same G3 shows at the same place in repeat bar 132 (10.5 dB, missing from the rendering there too), and Basic Pitch detects 55.

The stem's D4 stays about 11 dB below the real attacks at 102.345 and 102.743 and only wobbles by 1-2 dB, so there is no re-attack. gaps and gaps_paper are 0, Basic Pitch hears nothing, and only fl responds. What remains is the earlier D4 still ringing.

The stem's Bb3 decays steadily from its attack at 102.744 (11.9, 9.2, 8.7, 5.2 dB at 102.924, then 3.4 and -5.1) with no rise. gaps and gaps_paper are 0. The tab note is just the earlier Bb3 cut in two.

The stem shows a clear new G3 onset: 6.7 dB, rising 18.5 dB (h2 +19.9), with the residual 18 dB weaker. G3 is not a harmonic of the F2 or B3 around it, and Basic Pitch detects 55 at +1 ms. The repeat bar 116 (91.562) shows the same G3 onset (+21 dB) beside the tabbed B3, so the tab misses the G3 in both bars.

The stem E3 steps from -14 to -1 dB at about 112.03 and forms a separate spectral peak at 52 that is not Bb3's skirt. The rendering (-13 to -20 dB) and residual (-24 dB) are far weaker there. gaps and fl give 0.78 and 0.56, and Basic Pitch detects 52 at +4 ms, forming an E3-Bb3 C7 shell.

The stem's Bb3 decays steadily from 8.8 dB (122.95) through 7.9, 4.6 and 3.8 dB with no new rise near 123.04. Bb2 and its harmonics (70, 82) show no re-attack either. This looks like one chord split into two tab notes; the second is a duplicate and an overtone of the ringing Bb2.

The stem's F3 stays flat at about 2.3 dB (+2.5 dB rise) after the 122.909 attack. Meanwhile the residual jumps to 6.5 dB (+23 dB) at exactly this time, so the model detections are leakage from another instrument. This is not a guitar re-strike.

The stem shows only a roughly 100 ms broadband burst, equal at C3 and C#3 (3.9 and 3.2 dB), with no sustained pitched C#3. That burst matches a residual burst 11-12 dB louder (C#3 at 14.9 dB), so it is leakage. fl gives 0.03 and Basic Pitch finds nothing; the chromatic walking bass line is the only argument for keeping it.

This is a light strum at beat 1.2 (the onsets in beat 1 are evenly spaced about 80 ms apart). Basic Pitch detects Bb3 at 125.306, gaps gives 0.50 and fl 0.42. Bb3's harmonics rise slightly around 125.27-125.29 (70, 82, 89), while the D#4-only harmonics do not. The fundamental's level stays flat, so the evidence is weak.

guards: a fix that would force the fingering to drop a note nobody flagged is reduced to its removal
